---
title: "Build a Simple Agent-Based Model"
subtitle: "Translating a social-learning mechanism into Agents.jl"
toc: true
---

This chapter reorganizes the understood vector-based simulation as a small model in Agents.jl.

## Planned learning outcomes

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. Define agent-based modeling in terms of agents, state, rules, interaction, activation, time, and system-level outcomes.
2. Activate a Julia project environment and load the packages required by the model.
3. Explain how `Project.toml` and `Manifest.toml` support reproducibility.
4. Read a small agent definition without mastering Julia's full type system.
5. Distinguish agent properties from model-level parameters.
6. Write an initialization function that constructs and populates a model.
7. Write an `agent_step!` function that changes an agent's state.
8. Create and advance a discrete-time model.
9. Inspect the model and its agents.
10. Explain the model code line by line and connect it to conceptual modeling decisions.

## Planned scope

Each agent will have one substantive property: whether it has adopted a practice. Agents will be well mixed. During activation, an agent will randomly observe another agent, and a non-adopter may copy an adopter according to a model parameter.

The well-mixed interaction structure is an assumption, not a neutral default. A network-based interaction structure belongs to a later extension rather than this first model.

## Culminating activity

The learner will run the model for several steps, inspect how agent states change, and map the implemented components back to the earlier vector-based mechanism.
